annotation_description: Gem3F Heckler had Stern Scolding in hand, which counters creature spells with power or toughness 2 or less. Fallaji Archaeologist is a 0/3 creature — its toughness is 3, which is greater than 2, so Stern Scolding cannot target it. However, its power is 0, which is 2 or less, so Stern Scolding CAN target it (the condition is 'power or toughness 2 or less', meaning either stat being ≤2 qualifies). Allowing Fallaji Archaeologist to resolve lets the opponent mill cards and potentially get a card back or a +1/+1 counter. While Fallaji Archaeologist is not a major threat, using Stern Scolding to counter it would have been a clean 1-for-1 trade, and the card in hand (Goblin Charbelcher) needs 4 mana to cast plus 3 to activate, so protecting against the opponent's development while still having Snapback as backup would have been reasonable. That said, saving Stern Scolding for a more impactful target like another Psychic Frog or Death's Shadow is also defensible.

Kimi25 has 3 lands in hand (Island, 2x Watery Grave) and only needs one land drop. Discarding extra lands to Psychic Frog before combat would add permanent +1/+1 counters and increase combat damage, while the Frog's combat damage trigger would draw replacement cards. The Archaeologist is summoning sick and can't block, so the Frog connects freely. Discarding 1-2 excess lands pre-combat is essentially free value.
human_notes: No particular reason to cycle precombat, there's no spell in the deck worth casting precombat. Defensible to discard to frog or cycle it during declare blockers, but not a blunder to hold it.

annotation_description: With zero lands in play, discarding Fallaji Archaeologist (costs 1U) over Whir of Invention (costs XU​UU, essentially uncastable without lands) seems questionable. Archaeologist is much more castable if a land is found, provides a blocker body against threatening Psychic Frogs, and offers card selection through milling. Whir requires at minimum UUU which is extremely difficult to achieve with no lands.

annotation_description: With Death's Shadow attacking as a 4/4 (the largest threat), the 0/3 Fallaji Archaeologist should have been used to block it, preventing 4 damage. Instead, the blocking arrangement allowed more damage through than necessary. Blocking Death's Shadow with Archaeologist and a Frog with Thundertrap Trainer would have minimized damage to 2 (two unblocked 1-power creatures).
